newsitem.title: UK: Rotterdam refinery profits hit 7-month high near $3.
newsitem.headline: Rotterdam refinery profits hit 7-month high near $3.

text.p: Profit margins at oil refineries mostly edged higher in the West in the last week, led by Rotterdam which surged to seven-month highs, according to Reuters data using standard product yields.
But margins fell sharply in Singapore, losing some 40 cents a barrel due mostly to a big drop in gas oil against Dubai crude.
In the West margins are running above last month's average but in Singapore they are sharply lower and less than 20 percent of the peaks last spring.
In Rotterdam last week gasoline, gas oil and fuel oil gained 40 to 50 cents a barrel against Brent crude, boosting margins to seven-month highs.
Last Friday a refinery fully upgrading Brent made $2.96 a barrel compared to a previous peak of $3.62 last October.
Despite big gains in Rotterdam, profit margins in the Mediterranean slipped a few cents due mainly to a big drop in the value of gas oil.
Gas oil fell more than $1 a barrel compared to Urals crude which together with similar drop in gasoline values, more than offset modest gains in the value of high sulphur fuel.
On the U.S. Gulf Coast refiners enjoyed a pick up in profit margins although gains were pared at the end of the peak, according to the data.
There has been a slow upward trend in margins over the past six months despite a correction downwards in during much of April.
Last week heating oil gained around 60 cents a barrel compared to Brent which offset modest losses on gasoline and low sulphur fuel oil.
In Singapore cracking margins lost about 40 cents a barrel in the week to last Friday, mostly due to $1.10 a barrel drop in the value of gas oil compared to Dubai crude oil.
High sulphur fuel managed to make small gains but gasoline was down 20 cents a barrel against Dubai.
